title: Yandex Open-Sources 80B AliceAI-Foundation Under Apache 2.0
summary: Yandex releases AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, an 80B MoE model trained on 17.5T tokens. Apache 2.0 licensed with 88.7% pass@8 on IMO-AnswerBench.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Yandex open-sourced AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, an 80B total / 3B active MoE model trained on 17.5 trillion tokens under Apache 2.0.
- The base checkpoint scores 88.7% pass@8 on IMO-AnswerBench and 82.9% on LiveCodeBench, outperforming several competing MoE architectures.
- Yandex positions the release as an experimental testbed combining Kimi Delta Attention and Muon optimizer for future unified reasoning systems.


Yandex has released AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, an 80-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts transformer trained from scratch on 17.5 trillion tokens and licensed under Apache 2.0 for commercial use. The base checkpoint scores 88.7% pass@8 on IMO-AnswerBench and 82.9% on LiveCodeBench v5-v6, positioning it among the strongest open-weight MoE models available today. Officially released on November 26, 2026, the model combines novel architectural choices, including Kimi Delta Attention and the Muon optimizer, that Yandex says will inform a future unified reasoning system.


## Architecture and Training Pipeline


AliceAI-Foundation uses a mixture-of-experts design with 80 billion total parameters and roughly 3 billion active parameters per forward pass. The technical report describes a pretraining schedule that ran 17.5 trillion tokens through general domain data, followed by two context-extension stages and a dedicated phase for reasoning and agentic interaction. Yandex reports a final context window of 262,000 tokens, though the abstract does not specify the exact length used during each training stage.


The architecture integrates Kimi Delta Attention alongside full attention layers and introduces an auxiliary loss on MoE outputs to stabilize training dynamics. The team trained the model using the Muon optimizer, a recently published second-order method designed to accelerate convergence in large-scale transformer runs. These choices reflect Yandex's emphasis on architectural experimentation rather than a production-ready assistant, with the company framing the release as a testbed for components that will feed into future reasoning models.


## Benchmark Performance


On standard English-language evaluations, AliceAI-Foundation posts 88.7% pass@8 on IMO-AnswerBench, a measure of mathematical reasoning at International Mathematical Olympiad difficulty, and 82.9% pass@8 on LiveCodeBench v5-v6, a coding task suite that samples problems from recent competitive programming contests. The technical report also introduces two new Russian-language benchmarks: WikiWebFacts, which evaluates factual retrieval, and HardMultiQA, a multi-hop question-answering dataset.


- AliceAI-Foundation: 86.5% (WikiWebFacts), 67.9% (HardMultiQA)
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base (284B total / 13B active): 83.2%, 65.4%
- Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base: 72.8%, 54.5%


The results suggest that AliceAI-Foundation delivers competitive reasoning and coding performance despite its smaller active-parameter count, though the paper does not report latency or throughput comparisons that would clarify the efficiency trade-offs in production settings.


## Licensing and Release Details


Yandex has published the model weights, technical report, and training details to arXiv and made the checkpoint available under the[Apache 2.0 license](https://emergent.sh/glossary/apache-20-license) . This permissive license allows commercial deployment, derivative works, and redistribution without reciprocal open-sourcing requirements, a significant departure from the research-only licenses that govern many recent large-language-model releases from Chinese labs. The move positions AliceAI-Foundation as a viable base for startups and enterprises building vertical applications on top of open-weight architectures.


The release arrives on the same day as several other open-weight model announcements, including Ant Group's 560B medical MoE and Alibaba's Qwen4-Max, reflecting sustained momentum in the[open-source AI](https://emergent.sh/glossary/open-source-model) ecosystem. Yandex has not announced an instruction-tuned or chat variant of AliceAI-Foundation, though the technical report notes that the reasoning and agentic interaction stage included synthetic dialogue data that could support supervised fine-tuning in future iterations.


## What This Means


AliceAI-Foundation-80B represents a strategic bet that architectural innovation at the base-model layer can unlock gains in reasoning and long-context performance without requiring frontier-scale parameter counts. By open-sourcing the checkpoint under Apache 2.0, Yandex invites external teams to validate the Kimi Delta Attention and Muon optimizer choices on new domains and benchmarks, potentially accelerating the feedback loop between research and production deployment. For developers evaluating open-weight MoE models, AliceAI-Foundation offers a high-performance baseline with a clear path to commercial use, though teams will need to weigh the absence of instruction tuning and safety alignment against the model's strong base capabilities.
